mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not lead to tighter monetary policy within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a single month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or PAYEMS decline does not correlate with economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of periods with sustained HOUST increase, or correlation between HOUST and consumer demand weakens (Pearson r < 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decline does not correlate with supply chain disruption indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, the combination signals a tight labor market and restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy and labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between FEDFUNDS and UNRATE does not predict negative returns (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points month-over-month signals economic distress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase does not correlate with economic distress indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of periods with sustained RSAFS decline, or correlation between RSAFS and consumer demand weakens (Pearson r < 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, the combination signals a recessionary environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ < 0 for 2 quarters and FEDFUNDS > 2%
regime_hint: recessionary environment with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between GDPC1 and FEDFUNDS does not predict negative returns (Rank IC < 0.05).
